notes.text: Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: Jordan Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 68% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 62 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Nikolaj Ehlers (17 of 20 changes).

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 6 games cover only 20% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 49%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Cam York is day to day (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-four defenseman. Travis Sanheim has taken his spot beside Jamie Drysdale.
Travis Konecny is day to day (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward.

PHI.head: The Flyers have a hill to climb
PHI.body: Even though Philadelphia has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flyers can pull it off if they get good looks.

CAR.head: The Hurricanes should have the upper hand
CAR.body: Even though Philadelphia has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Flyers’ way back in is getting good looks.

story.head: The Flyers are still looking for their first win
paras: The Flyers are still looking for their first win of the season, 0-4-2 through six games. The Hurricanes have won four straight. The Canes already played in Philadelphia once this season and left with a 3-2 overtime win.
The Hurricanes shoot a lot, and the Flyers give up plenty. Expect plenty of hitting.
